card.decision: When the text contains no words (empty or whitespace-only), should longest_word raise ValueError or return the empty string?

experts.why: P-errors is the documented principle and the ticket leaves the choice open.
Bad input should fail loudly at the call site; a sentinel hides the case.
A blank input is bad input under P-errors; pytest.raises pins it precisely.
Callers find the mistake early, and P-errors matches this.

options.consequence: Blank input fails at the call site; callers must guard. A test asserts the raise. Can be changed later, but every caller is affected by a switch.
options.label: Raise ValueError

options.consequence: Blank input returns '' as a valid answer; the docstring must say so. Callers cannot tell 'no words' from a real empty result without checking. Breaks the spirit of P-errors unless the owner decides no-words is not bad input.
options.label: Return ''

ticket.purpose: Add a new module `src/longest.py` with `longest_word(text)` returning the longest word in `text`. Reuse the existing `words` helper from `src/textstats.py`.
ticket.title: Add longest_word

card.while_waiting: This ticket is parked at plan; other tickets continue.
card.why: Ticket 'Add longest_word' reserves this for the owner. src/textstats.py words() returns [] for blank text, so longest_word must branch explicitly. P-errors says bad input raises ValueError and never returns a sentinel.
